hardening_notes: proxy.ts:145 reads the whole JSON body in the proxy when Content-Length is absent (chunked upload), because a missing header is treated as 0. Only authenticated sessions reach it and Next bounds the buffered body, but a missing or non-numeric Content-Length should skip the check.

lib/seguranca/entrada.ts:37 uses `pilha.push(...v)`. A JSON array with more elements than the engine's spread-argument limit (reachable inside the 2 MB cap, e.g. an array of single digits) throws RangeError outside the try/catch, and the proxy answers 500 to that authenticated caller's own request. Push in a loop instead and wrap the walk in a try/catch that fails open.

The proxy JSON guard keys on Content-Type containing application/json and on Content-Length <= 2 MB. A JSON body sent with another content type, or a larger one, skips it and hits the earlier database 500. Not a boundary, but routes that write user text still need their own validation.

docker-compose.prod.yml:136 and hostgator-setup-kit/_common.sh pin WAHA by version tag (devlikeapro/waha:latest-2026.9.2) while serverless-redis-http, wacalls and asterisk are pinned by sha256 digest. update.sh now moves the whole installed base to this tag, so a digest pin would bind what the CI check in trivy.yml actually tested.

.github/workflows/trivy.yml scans the WAHA image by a hardcoded literal (devlikeapro/waha:latest-2026.9.2) rather than the $IMG value read from the compose file, so on the next bump the scan can silently keep covering the old version.

Dockerfile, Dockerfile.worker and Dockerfile.scheduler use floating base tags (node:22-alpine, alpine:3.20) and now `apk upgrade --no-cache`, so two builds of the same commit can differ. Acceptable for patching, but digest-pinned bases with scheduled bumps would make what Trivy scanned match what is published.
next.config.ts CSP has no script-src or connect-src (deliberate and documented), so it gives no XSS mitigation; the frame, object and base restrictions are the only effect.
redis:7-alpine and caddy:2-alpine in docker-compose.prod.yml are floating tags with the default pull policy (older than this scope).
seguranca.yml tails /tmp/app.log into the public job log on failure. Whether the app can log the Anthropic key or request headers there was not traced; worth confirming the logger never prints it.

local_checks.invariant: A scheduled message can be created, read, edited or cancelled only by a member (agent or above for writes) who can see the conversation under RLS, and service-role writes are bound to the session organization rather than the body.
local_checks.result: Holds. POST and PATCH read the conversation with the session client (conversaVisivel, RLS conversations_select via the three-argument fn_can_view_conversation) before any service-role write. Every insert, update and delete filters organization_id from authz.org.orgId. PATCH and DELETE load the row through the RLS-scoped session client bound to both path ids, require creator or manager, and update conditionally on status='agendada'. The table grants only SELECT to authenticated, and its select policy requires a visible conversation. The chatbot flow id from the body is checked against the session organization.

local_checks.invariant: The worker sends a scheduled item once, inside the row's tenant, and only while the scheduling user is still an active member with a sending role and the contact is neither blocked nor anonymized.
local_checks.result: Holds for tenant binding, single send and role/revocation. The claim is a conditional update on (organization_id, id, status='agendada'). The context query re-reads the membership (revoked_at null, accepted_at not null, role in agent/manager/admin) and the contact flags at send time, and the flow is re-read by organization. Anonymization deletes pending rows by trigger. Residual gap, recorded as hardening: the worker does not re-check that the scheduler can still see the conversation.

local_checks.invariant: Hiding a conversation or starring a message can only touch rows the caller can see in their own tenant.
local_checks.result: Holds. Both routes require agent or above and write with the session client filtered by the session organization. For conversations, the route first reads the row through RLS and returns 404 when it is not visible. For messages, the UPDATE has a WHERE and RETURNING, so messages_select (which requires a visible conversation) applies alongside messages_update and the restrictive messages_update_de_atendente policy. 'Hidden' is an inbox filter, not an access boundary. The 0510 trigger function is not security definer and updates only the same organization and conversation.

local_checks.invariant: A direct team-chat message is readable only by its author and recipient within the organization, and the sender cannot forge the author, the tenant or a recipient outside the organization.
local_checks.result: Holds. All reads use the session client. The equipe_mensagens_select policy requires organization membership and (general room, or author = auth.uid(), or recipient = auth.uid()), so a manager or admin cannot read other people's direct messages through this path. The 'com' parameter is validated as the literal 'geral' or a UUID before it is interpolated into the PostgREST .or() filter, so there is no filter injection. Inserts use the service role with organization_id and autor_user_id taken from the session, and the recipient is checked against non-revoked members of the session organization. Read markers are keyed to the session user. Authenticated has SELECT only on both tables.

local_checks.invariant: Automatic reassignment and the conversation/variable settings act only inside the event's or session's organization, and settings writes need manager or above.
local_checks.result: Holds. The handler filters every read, RPC and insert by row.organization_id and checks the configured flow against that organization. The signature route changes only the caller's own user metadata.

hardening_notes: lib/agendadas/executar.ts: at send time the worker re-checks the scheduler's membership and role but not whether they can still see the conversation (made private, or reassigned in visibility_mode 'own'). hardening_notes: Add an aggregate cap per webchat channel and per organization on new visitors per window (new contacts and conversations), independent of IP and token, and move these counters to the shared Redis limiter so they hold across replicas.

Derive the client IP from the hop written by the trusted proxy (rightmost untrusted element, or X-Real-IP set by the proxy) rather than the leftmost X-Forwarded-For value; getIp's fallback to 127.0.0.1 puts all header-less requests in one bucket.

lerCorpoDoBalao only rejects an oversized body up front when Content-Length is declared. For chunked bodies it buffers up to the framework cap before the 8 KB check. Read the stream with a running byte counter and abort at 8 KB.
The Origin allow-list is a browser-side control only: a non-browser client can send any Origin header. The UI and docs should not present it as protection against scripted senders.
origemPermitida ignores the scheme, so http://<allowed-domain> is accepted. Consider requiring https outside localhost.

If an attendant merges a webchat contact into another contact, the visitor's next message creates a second contact and conversation with the same provider_conversation_id. lerDoVisitante's maybeSingle then errors and the widget gets 500. Reuse the existing conversation by provider_conversation_id first.

A visitor can set any unclaimed email on their own webchat contact, and email is unique per organization. A stranger can therefore pre-claim a real customer's email on a throwaway contact. Consider keeping visitor-typed email in source_metadata only, until an attendant confirms it.
The visitor token stays in localStorage with no expiry. On a shared computer the next person on the same site sees the earlier chat. Consider an expiry or a 'end conversation' control in the widget.

local_checks.invariant: The per-IP limit on the public webchat routes is keyed on a value the requester cannot choose.
local_checks.result: getIp returns the first comma-separated element of X-Forwarded-For, else req.ip, else 127.0.0.1. The shipped Caddyfile uses plain reverse_proxy with no trusted_proxies; Caddy's handling of a client-sent header there is its own default, not visible in source. The CloudPanel runbook's nginx vhost sets X-Forwarded-For to $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for, which appends to the client-sent header, so the first element would be requester-controlled there. docker-compose.traefik.yml does not configure forwarded-header trust; the hosting panel's Traefik is outside source. The limiter is an in-process Map, so it is per replica.

local_checks.invariant: Rows created by anonymous visitors are bounded per channel or tenant, not only per requester-chosen identity.
local_checks.result: The only bounds are 60/min per IP key and 15/min per visitor-token hash. The token is generated by the requester, so each request can carry a fresh one. Each accepted request with a fresh token inserts a contact, a conversation (fn_upsert_wa_conversation), a message, attempts a lead (garantirLeadDaConversa) and emits ai_agent.dispatch_requested. There is no per-channel or per-organization cap, and no proof-of-work or challenge. Even with a truthful IP, one address can create 60 contacts, conversations and lead attempts per minute.
